headline: Approved an emergency committee to draft public access guidelines for Ferdinando, Corneliusen, Martin and Ball properties.
summary: Representatives of the Ferdinando family said new food safety rules limit public walking trails and dog roaming on their farm fields. A new committee led by Chairman Riccardo Buzzanga will look for a temporary fix, which will likely include signage. The group also approved signage changes for Ashleigh Drive and accepted a $260.85 reimbursement.
decisions: Approved the minutes of July 13, 2026, unanimously.
Approved an emergency Ad Hoc Committee to prepare public access guidelines for the Ferdinando, Corneliusen, Martin and Ball properties, with all seven members voting yes.
Approved the committee's membership: Buzzanga as chair, Chabot and Spoerl as members, and Foote and Carver as liaisons, with all seven members voting yes.
Approved the signage changes for Ashleigh Drive, unanimously.
Accepted a $260.85 check from the New Hampshire Association of Conservation Commissions as reimbursement for BioBlitz day, unanimously.
Voted to seal the minutes of the nonpublic session, 7-0.

DERRY CONSERVATION COMMISSION
MunicipalCenter
Derry, NH
August17,2026
-Call to Order: Chairman Buzzanga called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m., he led the Pledgeof
Allegiance.
-Roll Call: Riccardo Buzzanga, Rick Metts, Robert Spoerl, Eileen Chabot. Jay Hildreth, Cheryl Holbert,
Pam Pirro,Linda Comrie, Katherine Arbour, Christopher Morlock, Council Liaison Charlie Foote and Land
Manager Elizabeth Carver.
-Chairs Report: Chairman Buzzanga announced Commissioner Connolly has moved to a new area and
willno longer be able to serve on the Board. He wishedher well in her new community.
-Correspondence: Chairman Buzzanga updated he hadreceived a letterfrom Jacob and Sarah White
regarding a property that was recently purchased at 1 Feather Bed Lane. She shared wildlifesightings on
the land siteand has asked the Commission to doits due diligence. Land Manager, Beth Carver, will
follow up with a letter.There were reports of alleged violations at 54 Beaver Land Avenue, Tax Map 51 Lot
75 and at 19 Whitney’s Grove Tax Map 15 Lot 16-4. The Commission also received a renewal fora
Groundwater Release Detection Permit for B& H Oil at 36 South Main Street.
-Approval of Minutes:
 
Commissioner Metts MOVED to approve the Minutes of July 13, 2026. Commissioner Holbert
Seconded the Motion. Vote: Unanimous   
-Chairman Buzzanga asked Commissioner Comrie tosit infor Commissioner Connolly.
-Site Plan Review: 38 Jackman Road/Jackman Road Right-of-Way; Tax Map 7 Lot 77; Owner: Joe
Mastriano, 3 Ball Avenue, Salem New Hampshire 03079; Surveyor: LavelleAssociates Hampstead NH
and Engineer: Brad Eric,Bradanese Engineering Alliance,Inc.Saugus Massachusetts.
-EricBradanese, PE of Engineering Alliance and siteowner Joe Mastriano provided a presentation forthe
project. Mr. Bradanese described thelot as 6.3 acres. The owner has received varianceto build a single-
family dwelling on this Class 6 Road. It willbe maintained by the property owners along Jackman Road.
Mr. Bradanese has metwith the Technical Review Committee whereit was broughtto theirattention that
there isa prime wetland onthe property located at the top of plans. There isalso a secondary wetland
down on theleft side shown on the plan that runs through the middle of the property. He showed on the
plan wherethere isa 150-foot setbackto the primary wetland and a 75-foot buffer zone. The siteruns
past the Rockingham RecreationalTrail.There isa secondary building proposedin these plans, forthe
future,not to be builtwithin this permit. The proposal includes improvements to Jackman Road which
1
include a 20-foot-widegravel road that willbe designed to meet the town engineered standardsfora
Class 6 road. The added 2 feet of gravelwillhelp waterto directlyinfiltrateto avoid creating any storm
water issues. The only area to accessthe property isshown on the map. The FireDepartment has
requested a hammerhead turnaround to allowfor a fireengine to pullin, back up and pullout. Asecond
turnaroundis required and shown on the map. Mr. Bradanese further explained that the driveway access
can only be provided by pullingitas far away as possible from the prime wetland, whichis within 75-to-
100-foot buffers to the prime wetland. The entiretyof the frontage on Jackman Roadis within 150 feet of
the wetland. They proposeto maintain a very similar grading scheme as to whatis currentlyon Jackman
Road now.
-Chairman Buzzanga asked howthe Class 6 road would transitionwith the RailTrailentrance and then
restartas a road. Mr. Bradanese spoke of the custom-built gates that willhave locks. Both Fireand Police
Departments will always have access andkeys to accessthe trails. They have been working with the New
Hampshire Trail Bureau regarding the gates and entry.The public willstillhave accessto therail trailvia
man passon the sides of the gates. The pittesting and septic testingwere conducted for 6 bedrooms. All
the workfor the single family isoutside of the 75-foot bufferwith the exception of one small section to
allow forthe requested secondfire apparatus turnaround perimeter. The Commissioners asked about the
30-foot pipe shown on the plans.
-Chairman Buzzanga believed the plan would be brought before the Commission again and spoke of
what he thought they would need to plan accordingly. When this plan isbrought back, the Commission
would schedule a site walk, and a second meeting would entail a conversation of the site walk
observations, questions or concerns. A possible thirdmeeting could be anticipated. Chairman Buzzanga
highlighted what documents Mr. Bradanese should bring to the next meeting for review by the
Commissioners.
-Public Use of the Corneliusen, Martin, Fernando and Ball Properties: Representatives from the
Ferdinando familyAndrew Chisholm of Hampstead New Hampshire and Melissa Ferinando of Derry, New
Hampshire came before the Commission to speak about the FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMS)
Program of 2023. This program includes safety protocols that help to prevent contamination of food as
well as shiftingthe focus from responding to foodborne illness to preventing it.They had sent
communication with regard to concernsthat they have with what is happening within theirproperties;
Properties that the Conservation Commission has easements on, and properties the Commission are
stakeholders of.Their letterrefersto dog waste and howthat canaffect vegetables and theirbusiness.
Ferdinando Farmsis of a certain size that must be in compliance with FSMS. Mr. Chisholm states that
within the guidelines of the FSMS Manual, there are restrictionson public accessto the food or food
supply areas. He referred to the current issues happening with foodborne pathogens in the country. They
wouldlike to mitigate that from happening. They referredto the walkingtrails published inthe kiosks,
specificallyat the end of English Range Road and Holiday Avenue. One published trailmoves directly
through the corn fieldsand pumpkin fields.Other public walking trailsgo around the corn silage which a
food supplyfor the beef cattleand follows throughto a haysilo and electricfence. To stay in compliance,
2
they can no longerallow the public to walk throughthese areas/fields and allow dogs to roamfree. Ms.
Ferdinandostates these are new laws sheis dealing with and states they were not aware there were
walking trailsthrough anyof thefields forthe public.
Chairman Buzzanga suggests a Subcommittee be created to addressthis issue in a timely manner. The
Subcommittee willdevelop binding recommendations for the process. Commissioner Spoerl talked
aboutthe other stakeholders, the amendment of easement language and council review. Chairman
Buzzanga spoke of the Commissions’ authority to make emergency changes now. To reach an immediate
solution to this problem, Chairman Buzzanga suggest acting now to prevent problems. He volunteers to
Chair that committee along with Commissioner Chabot, Commissioner Spoerl and Land Manager Beth
Carver. They willcome up with a temporary solution whichwill likelyinclude signage.
 
Commissioner Metts MOVES to establish an emergency Ad Hoc Committee to prepare guidelines for
the Ferdinando, Corneliusen, Martin and Ball properties,using the FSMS regulations to form guidelines
for public accessto the aforementioned properties. Cheryl Holbert seconds the MOTION.

At 7:00 p.m., Commissioner Metts MOVES to open a Public Hearing. Commissioner Chabot seconded
the Motion.   
-Greg Boiko, Jewell Lane: Mr. Boiko shares concerns regarding the townforest that his property abuts.
He has concernsregarding the building happening at 12 Jewell Lane. Conversation ensues and Chairman
Buzzanga suggests Mr. Boiko email him to hear the matterfurther.
 
At 7:04 p.m., Commissioner Metts Motionsto close the Public Hearing. Commissioner Chabot
seconds the Motion.

-Committee and Liaison Reports

and friends to discuss and celebrate the amazing gardens.

earlierinthe week. They spoke with people whowere new to the community andfolks who wouldlike to
help out with trailmaintenance.
-State Compliance: Commissioner Chabot reviewed a passage from the New Hampshire Association of
Conservation Commissions (NHACC) newsletter of the month. It spoke about what the Conservation
Commissions’ role isin Land Management. Commissioner Chabot spoke of natural resource inventories
and forestry management plans. The Annual Meeting of the NHACC is scheduled for Saturday, November
7, 2026, at Pembroke Academy. Keynote speakers from the Hubbard Brook Ecosystem Study, an
important New Hampshire initiative willbe attending. Wetlands Permit Application fees have been
increasedfrom $400 to $600 dueto the passageof the 2026/2027 StateBudget. The Departmentof
Environmental Services (DES)will be launching a new modern online portalthat willeventually take the
place of the Onestop database.
-Property Management: Chairman Buzzanga updated that he and Ms.Carver continue to complete
tasks. He thanked Derry Public Works Department for theircontinued responsiveness to the
Commission.
-Land Maintenance: Commissioner Spoerl updated scheduled trailcleanup had been rained out but
discussions were held regarding what information should belisted in the kiosks.
-Reporting Compliance- No updates.
-Land Acquisition: No updates.
-Council Liaison Report: There are no current updates.
-Land Manager Report: Ms. Carver updated the Community Wildfire Protection Plan willbe presented at
a Public Hearing at the Town Council Meeting scheduled for September 15, 2026. Parkland Medical
Center has a groupof volunteers who have askedto help to pull the bittersweet at Broadview. Proposed

with trailclean-ups. On Friday,September 18, 2026, Matt Tarrof the UNH Extension willlead a tourof
Broadview. Some Commissioners voices concernsover D.E.S. notifications.20-day notices are intended
4
forthe recipients and not the Commissioners. A fallentree at Broadview was removed by D.P.W.It was
used as a training opportunity. A request from the Maine Botanical Garden wasreceived to collect seeds
of four-leaved milkweed at a Conservation property. Ms. Carver explained the processto furtherthe
species. A requestfor metal detecting at Broadview wasreceived. This has presented an opportunity for
the Commission to adoptregulations. This willbe discussed at a latermeeting. A meeting washeld to
discuss the languagefor signage concerningthe property at Ashleigh Drive with the stakeholders.
Discussion ensued.
 
Commission Metts MOVED to approvethe signage changes for Ashleigh Drive. Commissioner Holbert
seconded the MOTION. Vote: Unanimous  
-Ms. Carver updated the Land & Water Conservation Fund conducted a visit to Corneliusen, Coal Marsh,

-Other Business: Chairman Buzzanga updated Linda Comrie has expressed interestto becoming full
